messages:
maya: FYI Customer AC-451 reporting traffic from Amsterdam hitting our us-west anycast. High p95 (~1.8s) and occasional 502/403. They saw repeated retries.
alex: thanks. can you paste their repro steps + any DNS results?
carlos: customer sent this snippet. curl connects to 34.82.10.12 (us-west) and returns 502 sometimes, 403 other times. response header shows `x-region: us-west-1`.

# customer curl
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\"
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (34.82.10.12) port 443
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< x-region: us-west-1

# dig from office (NL-ISP)
$ dig +short api.redwood.ai @their-isp
34.82.10.12
TTL: 43200

# edns client subnet
$ dig @their-isp api.redwood.ai +edns=0 +subnet=78.48.0.0/24
;; ANSWER SECTION:
api.redwood.ai. 43200 IN A 34.82.10.12

sam: authoritative now shows api.redwood.ai CNAME -> api-eu.redwood.ai (TTL 60) -> eu anycast A 18.194.66.19

alex: so recursive resolver returned a stale A (TTL 43200) pointing to us-west. possible causes: long-lived cache at ISP, resolver ignoring authoritative TTL changes, or our anycast BGP changes leaving stale route in certain PoPs.

support-bot: incident created RED-7033, assigned eng-infra, priority P1.

maya: customer also reports billing spikes due to client retries on 502s. billing looped in.
billing-team: please provide time windows and request ids; we'll review credits.

sam: quick triage we should ask customer to run:
1) `dig +short api.redwood.ai @1.1.1.1` and `@8.8.8.8`
2) `dig +short api.redwood.ai @their-isp` (confirm TTL)
3) `dig +edns=0 +subnet=0.0.0.0/0 @their-isp` (EDNS check)
4) `curl --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:18.194.66.19 https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health` (force EU IP)
5) traceroute to the resolved IP

carlos: customer ran 1-3. Public resolvers returned EU IP; their ISP returned US IP with TTL 43180. EDNS showed no client-subnet.

alex: immediate mitigations:
- fastest: ask ISP NOC to purge their cache for api.redwood.ai (customer willing to escalate)
- short-term: ask customer to use region alias `api.eu.redwood.ai` (no code change if DNS name configurable)
- server-side hotfix: enable per-account region pinning in edge LB to override DNS -> route requests to EU regardless of DNS (feature-flagged)
- risky: TCP-level proxy from the us-west node to eu (not preferred)

maya: customer prefers zero code changes.
sam: then we should pursue ISP purge + LB override for AC-451. eng-infra can enable per-account override quickly.

alex: we have `route-override` flag in edge-proxy. plan:
1) enable override for AC-451 on eu-canary
2) observe auth success and p95 for 20-30m
3) if stable, promote to eu-prod and monitor 24h

support-bot: route-override enabled for AC-451 on eu-canary at 1769704820 :white_check_mark:

carlos: customer re-ran curl — now resolves to EU IP and latency dropped to ~110ms; 403s/502s disappeared. customer confirmed improved UX.

billing-team: provisional credit approved for window 2026-03-09T08:45 -> 2026-03-09T10:10. please attach request ids.

maya: eng-infra action items:
- contact DNS provider and ask about replication delays and cache invalidation (RED-7034)
- confirm no stale BGP adverts in any PoPs (RED-7035)
- implement monitoring rule: alert when >0.5% of requests from a region resolve to non-local anycast IP (RED-7036)

alex: postmortem notes:
- our change last week included switching eu mapping; we didn't follow TTL-handshake (lower TTL long enough before change)
- add rollout checklist: set TTL=30s for 10mins -> change -> monitor resolver answers for anomalies -> revert TTL
- document guidance for customers: prefer explicit region aliases (api.<region>.redwood.ai) if they have strict residency needs

sam: also log these fields for any such incident: resolved_ip, resolver_name, resolver_ttl, edns_subnet, account_id, request_ids.

maya: creating follow-ups and closing after DNS provider response and billing credit posted. thanks team :thumbsup:\n
